instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: The Greek is the idiom of having in the womb: the woman will be with child. It is bodily conception, said of the virgin in the quoted prophecy. Verses: Mat 1:23.
observations.grounds: the virgin shall conceive and bear

observations.text: The Greek noun is the laying down of seed; with the next word it makes the phrase the English renders as the power to conceive, said of Sarah past the age. It names the act of conceiving, not a thought. Verses: Heb 11:11.
observations.grounds: received power to conceive

observations.text: The Greek noun is seed, the word that completes the phrase rendered the power to conceive in this verse; the English folds the pair into one verb. Verses: Heb 11:11.
observations.grounds: received power to conceive

observations.text: The Greek verb is to take together and so to conceive in the womb; the angel tells Mary she will conceive and bear a son. It is bodily conception. Verses: Luk 1:31.
observations.grounds: you will conceive in your womb

observations.text: In these two verses the Hebrew verb is bodily conception: Moses asks whether he conceived the people, and the angel tells the barren woman she will conceive. Verses: Num 11:12, Judg 13:3.
observations.grounds: Did I conceive all this people

observations.text: In these three verses the same verb is used figuratively: wicked people conceive trouble, chaff and mischief and give birth to evil, iniquity and stubble. The picture of pregnancy carries what is formed in a person and then brought out in act. Verses: Job 15:35, Isa 33:11, Isa 59:4.
observations.grounds: they conceive mischief and give birth

observations.text: The Hebrew verb is bodily conception, the angel's announcement of a son and the sign of the virgin; it is a promise of birth, not a thought. Verses: Judg 13:5, Judg 13:7, Isa 7:14.
observations.grounds: you shall conceive and bear a son

observations.text: The Hebrew verb is to be sown with seed: the woman cleared of defilement will be able to conceive children. It is bodily conception. Verses: Num 5:28.
observations.grounds: she shall be free and shall conceive

observations.text: The Hebrew verb is the warming that conceives: the psalmist says his mother conceived him in sin. It is bodily conception, with sin placed at its start. Verses: Psa 51:5.
observations.grounds: in sin did my mother conceive me

observations.text: In these two verses the Greek is a verb of looking; the phrase is that Jesus does not look at the face of men, which the English renders as caring for no one's opinion. It names regard for other people's standing, not a view of his own. Verses: Mat 22:16, Mar 12:14.
observations.grounds: do not care about anyone

observations.text: In Job 32 'opinion' is Elihu's own view or knowledge, which he is afraid at first to declare because of his youth and then insists on declaring. Verses: Job 32:6, Job 32:10, Job 32:17.
observations.grounds: let me also declare my opinion

observations.text: In Pro 18:2 the Hebrew is the word for heart, the fool's own mind: he takes pleasure only in revealing what his heart holds, which the English renders as his opinion. Verses: Pro 18:2.
observations.grounds: only in expressing his opinion

observations.text: In Rom 1:21 'thinking' is the reasonings of the mind, the plural inner deliberation that became futile when people knew God and did not honor him. Verses: Rom 1:21.
observations.grounds: became futile in their thinking

observations.text: In 2Cor 12:19 'thinking' is the readers assuming something, that Paul has been defending himself to them; the verse corrects it. Verses: 2Cor 12:19.
observations.grounds: Have you been thinking all along

observations.text: In 1Pe 4:1 'way of thinking' is the intent or mind-set believers are to arm themselves with, set beside Christ's suffering. Verses: 1Pe 4:1.
observations.grounds: arm yourselves with the same way

observations.text: In Rom 1:21 this code is the Greek conjunction in the clause about becoming futile in thinking; it joins clauses and carries no thinking, which G1261 carries. Verses: Rom 1:21.
observations.grounds: futile in their thinking

observations.text: In Heb 11:15 'thinking of' is keeping in mind or remembering the land they left; the verse says that if they had kept it in mind they could have returned. Verses: Heb 11:15.
observations.grounds: thinking of that land from which

observations.text: In Phili 1:17 'thinking' is supposing or intending: some preach out of ambition, expecting to add affliction to Paul in prison. Verses: Phili 1:17.
observations.grounds: thinking to afflict me in my

observations.text: In 1Cor 14:20 'thinking' is the mind or understanding, the Greek noun for the seat of understanding; believers are not to be children in it, but mature. Verses: 1Cor 14:20.
observations.grounds: do not be children in your thinking

observations.text: In these eight verses the Hebrew verb of saying introduces a thought quoted as a sentence: Jacob, David, Achish, the Jebusites, the king of Israel, Sennacherib, Nehemiah's enemies and the wicked each 'say' it in themselves. The thought is inner speech, usually about what others will do or what will not be seen. Verses: Gen 32:8, 1Sa 27:11, 1Sa 27:12, 2Sa 5:6, 2Ki 7:12, 2Ch 32:1, Neh 6:9, Psa 64:5.
observations.grounds: they talk of laying snares secretly

observations.text: In these seven verses 'thinks' is holding an estimate of oneself, that one has something, is wise, stands, is a prophet, is something, has confidence in the flesh, or is religious. Each time the verse tests the estimate and finds it wanting or sets another beside it. Verses: Luk 8:18, 1Cor 3:18, 1Cor 10:12, 1Cor 14:37, Gal 6:3, Phili 3:4, Jam 1:26.
observations.grounds: thinks that he is wise

observations.text: In Rom 14:14 'thinks it unclean' is the reckoning of the person: the thing is unclean for the one who counts it so, though nothing is unclean in itself. Verses: Rom 14:14.
observations.grounds: for anyone who thinks it unclean

observations.text: In 1Cor 7:36 'thinks' is judging his own conduct toward his betrothed to be improper; the Greek is a verb of holding as so, and the judgment is the man's own. Verses: 1Cor 7:36.
observations.grounds: If anyone thinks that he is not

observations.text: In 1Sa 20:3 'thinks' is the Hebrew verb of saying, quoting what Saul says in himself: that Jonathan must not know. It is inner speech about another person. Verses: 1Sa 20:3.
observations.grounds: Your father knows well that I have

observations.text: In 2Pe 1:13 this code is the Greek conjunction in the clause 'I think it right'; it carries no thinking, which the verb of G2233 carries. Verses: 2Pe 1:13.
observations.grounds: I think it right

observations.text: In these seven verses 'think' is a question put to a hearer for his view: 'What do you think?' asks Jesus, and the hearers are asked about a case, a person or a coming. It asks for a judgment the hearer already forms. Verses: Mat 17:25, Mat 18:12, Mat 21:28, Mat 22:17, Mat 22:42, Luk 10:36, Joh 11:56.
observations.grounds: What do you think about the Christ

observations.text: In these verses 'think' is holding a belief, often one the verse then corrects: the Gentiles' belief that many words are heard, the belief that Jesus cannot appeal to his Father, that he came to give peace, that the Galileans were worse, that the Scriptures give life apart from him, that killing believers serves God. In the Pauline verses it is Paul's own estimate of the apostles' place, of his judgment, of the body's parts and of the foolish. Verses: Mat 6:7, Mat 26:53, Luk 12:51, Luk 13:2, Luk 13:4, Joh 5:39, Joh 5:45, Joh 16:2, 1Cor 4:9, 1Cor 7:40, 1Cor 12:23, 2Cor 11:16, Heb 10:29.
observations.grounds: Do you think that I cannot appeal

observations.text: In Mat 9:4 'think evil' is to turn something over in the mind: Jesus asks why they entertain evil in their hearts, and the verse names the heart as the place. Verses: Mat 9:4.
observations.grounds: Why do you think evil in your hearts

observations.text: In 2Pe 1:13 'I think it right' is judging or counting it fitting: Peter counts it right to remind them while he lives. Verses: 2Pe 1:13.
observations.grounds: I think it right

observations.text: In 2Cor 12:6 'think more of me' is the estimate others form: Paul holds back lest anyone credit him with more than they see or hear. Verses: 2Cor 12:6.
observations.grounds: no one may think more of me

observations.text: In Phili 4:8 'think about these things' is a command to direct the mind to what is true, honorable and excellent: to reckon with them and dwell on them. Verses: Phili 4:8.
observations.grounds: think about these things

observations.text: In Eph 3:20 'think' is to take in with the mind, to conceive: God does more than all that we ask or conceive, set beside asking. Verses: Eph 3:20.
observations.grounds: all that we ask or think

observations.text: In these verses 'think' is to hold something as so: Jesus tells the hearers not to suppose he came to abolish the law or bring peace, Paul says God is not to be thought like an image, and Paul gives his own judgment on remaining as one is. In the first three the held notion is a wrong one the verse corrects; in 1Cor 7:26 it is a considered view. Verses: Mat 5:17, Mat 10:34, Act 17:29, 1Cor 7:26.
observations.grounds: Do not think that I have come

observations.text: In Rom 12:3 and Phili 3:15 'think' is the mind-set, the way one is minded: not to rate oneself above what is right but to be sober, and to hold the same mind or another. The verb names the direction of the mind, with a measure given. Verses: Rom 12:3, Phili 3:15.
observations.grounds: not to think of himself more highly

observations.text: In these four verses the Hebrew verb of saying is rendered 'think': the Assyrian asks whether words are strategy, the Chronicler accuses Israel of thinking to withstand the Lord, and the Spirit says so the house of Israel thinks. It is the inner or said claim of those addressed. Verses: 2Ki 18:20, 2Ch 13:8, Isa 36:5, Eze 11:5.
observations.grounds: Do you think that mere words are

observations.text: In Est 4:13 'think' is the Hebrew verb of imagining or supposing: Mordecai warns Esther not to imagine to herself that she alone will escape. Verses: Est 4:13.
observations.grounds: Do not think to yourself that

observations.text: In Psa 119:52 'think of' is to call to mind: the psalmist recalls the Lord's rules from of old and takes comfort. Verses: Psa 119:52.
observations.grounds: When I think of your rules

observations.text: In Isa 10:7 'think' is the Hebrew verb of planning and devising: the Assyrian's heart is not set on the plan the Lord has, for his own purpose is destruction of nations; the verb is of planning. Verses: Isa 10:7.
observations.grounds: his heart does not so think

observations.text: In these three verses 'think' is reckoning or counting: whether one holds a thing just, whether one would reckon the deep to be white-haired, and what God counts the son of man to be. Verses: Job 35:2, Job 41:32, Psa 144:3.
observations.grounds: Do you think this to be just

observations.text: In Job 6:26 and Jer 23:27 'think' is to plan or intend: Job asks whether his friends intend to reprove words, and the prophets intend to make the people forget the name. Verses: Job 6:26, Jer 23:27.
observations.grounds: who think to make my people forget
